questions.prompt: What does compaction do, in Anthropic's definition?

options.text: It compresses the tokens so the same text uses fewer of them in the window.
options.explanation: Compaction does not re-encode the text. It replaces old turns with a summary.

options.text: It summarizes old turns near the limit and continues from the summary.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic calls it the first lever in context engineering for long-term coherence.

options.text: It moves the conversation to a model with a larger context window.
options.explanation: The model stays the same. Compaction makes the context smaller instead.

questions.prompt: On Claude, who decides when compaction runs with compaction at a token threshold?

options.text: The API, when input tokens reach the trigger you set
options.explanation: Right. It is one parameter on your normal requests.

options.text: Your code, by sending a separate compaction request to the API
options.explanation: That describes compaction on demand, where your code decides.

options.text: The user, by pressing a button in the chat window
options.explanation: Threshold compaction runs inside the request that reaches the threshold, with no user step.

questions.prompt: After compaction, the cache-hit rate falls. What does OpenAI's prompt caching guide say?

options.text: Turn compaction off, because a lower hit rate always costs more.
options.explanation: OpenAI says fewer input tokens can still save money even when the cache-hit rate falls.

options.text: It is a bug in compaction that should be reported.
options.explanation: It is expected: compaction replaces earlier context, which can change the prefix.

options.text: This is expected; compare total input cost before and after.
options.explanation: Right. Compaction can change the prefix, so the first request after it may reuse less of the cache.
